dedupe_keys.name: oakbat oak ridge spoofing and interference test battery gnss rf recordings

description: The Oak Ridge Spoofing and Interference Test Battery (OAKBAT), published by Oak Ridge National Laboratory, is a set of recorded radio-frequency GNSS scenarios with spoofing and interference for testing receivers and detection methods, described by Albright, Powers, Bonior and Combs at ION GNSS+ 2020. Scenario series cover GPS and Galileo; the Galileo E1 series was the harvested record. Each recording is binary sampled RF data in the format given in the paper, and the project's GitHub organisation holds metadata, equipment documentation, configuration files, collection procedures and a full list of the RF files, so that the recordings can be reproduced independently. Coverage: laboratory scenarios, not places. Format and access: binary RF files through OSTI and ORNL's data service, free of charge as a US Department of Energy product. Caveats: synthetic attacks in a controlled setting; large files; receivers must replay the RF data. Simulation uses: benchmark scenarios to test how positioning and timing used by power, telecom and transport systems withstand spoofing and jamming, and to validate detection models. Related records: Jammertest gives open-air tests; the Laura Bassi dataset shows interference at sea; Kshana simulates PNT resilience.
